children.text: paraṃ parasyāḥ prakṛter anādim ekaṃ niviṣṭaṃ bahudhā guhāsu |
children.translated_text: The Supreme One, beyond the highest <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), beginningless, one, dwelling variously in the caves [of the heart],

children.text: sarvālayaṃ sarvacarācarasthaṃ tvām eva viṣṇuṃ śaranaṃ prapadye ||
children.translated_text: the abode of all, residing in all moving and unmoving beings — to You alone, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, I take refuge.

children.text: ātmāmburāśau nikhilo 'pi loko magno 'pi nācāmati nekṣate ca |
children.translated_text: Though the entire world is immersed in the ocean of the Self, it neither sips from it nor perceives it —

children.text: āścaryam etan mṛgatṛṣṇikābhe bhavāmburāśau ramate mṛṣaiva ||
children.translated_text: this is a wonder: in this ocean of existence, which is like a mirage, it delights vainly.
In the ocean of dwelling in the womb, birth, old age, death, and separation,

children.text: jagad ālokya nimagnaṃ prāha guruṃ prāñjaliḥ śiṣyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing the world submerged, the disciple, with folded hands, spoke to the teacher:
You are the knower of the <s>Vedas</s> with their limbs, the destroyer of the host of doubts, the speaker of truth;
O Blessed Lord, I ask a question about crossing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence).

children.text: dīrghe 'smin saṃsāre saṃsarataḥ kasya kena sambandhaḥ |
children.translated_text: In this long <s>saṃsāra</s>, for one who transmigrates, what is the connection of whom with what?

children.text: karma śubhāśubhaphaladam anubhavati gatāgatair iha kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who experiences <s>karma</s> that yields auspicious and inauspicious fruits through comings and goings here?
The <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), bound in the net of <s>karma</s> and <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), transmigrates like a silkworm.
How is there liberation from that bondage, from the dense darkness of delusion?
For one who knows the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self), <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> do not become binding.

children.text: iti gaditapūrvavākyaiḥ prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ ca me brūhi ||
children.translated_text: Thus, through the words spoken by the ancients, explain to me <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self).

children.text: ity ādhāro bhagavān pṛṣṭaḥ śiṣyeṇa taṃ sa hovāca |
children.translated_text: Thus asked by the disciple, the Blessed Lord <s>Ādhāra</s> (the Support) said to him:

children.text: viduṣām apy atigahanaṃ vaktavyam idaṃ śṛṇu tathāpi tvam ||
children.translated_text: What is to be spoken is extremely profound even for the learned; nevertheless, listen.

children.text: satyam iva jagad asatyaṃ mūlaprakṛter idaṃ kṛtaṃ yena |
children.translated_text: The world, though appearing as real, is unreal — it is created from the root <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature);
having bowed to <s>Upendra</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), I shall declare this essence of the highest truth (<s>Paramārthasāra</s>).

children.text: avyaktād aṇḍam abhūd aṇḍād brahmā tataḥ prajāsargaḥ |
children.translated_text: From the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>) arose the cosmic egg; from the egg arose <s>Brahmā</s>; from him, the creation of beings.

children.text: māyāmayī pravṛttiḥ saṃhriyata iyaṃ punaḥ kramaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This activity, consisting of <s>māyā</s> (illusion), is again withdrawn in due order.
Though consisting of <s>māyā</s> and insentient, the aggregate of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and organs performs actions;

children.text: tadadhiṣṭātā dehī sacetano 'pi na karoti kiṃcid api ||
children.translated_text: the embodied one who presides over it, though conscious, does nothing at all.

children.text: yadvad acetanam api san nikaṭasthe bhrāmake bhramati loham |
children.translated_text: Just as iron, though insentient, revolves when a magnet is nearby,
so too the aggregate of organs functions when the body is presided over by consciousness.

children.text: yadvat savitary udite karoti karmāṇi jīvaloko 'yam |
children.translated_text: Just as when the sun rises, this world of living beings performs its actions,

children.text: na ca tāni karoti ravir na kārayati tadvad ātmāpi ||
children.translated_text: yet the sun neither performs those actions nor causes them to be performed — so too is the Self (<s>Ātman</s>).
When the mind, overcome by <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), is animated by consciousness,
there arises in the deluded one the notion of personal identity, pleasure, and pain.
'I am the doer, the enjoyer, the seer of actions — superior and others' —
thus the Self, though all-pervading and pure by nature, falsely identifies [with these].
Just as a clear crystal takes on the color of various colored objects placed near it,

children.text: tadvad upādher guṇabhāvitasya bhāvaṃ vibhur dhatte ||
children.translated_text: so too the all-pervading [Self] takes on the character of the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) conditioned by the <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: gacchati gacchati salile dinakarabimbaṃ sthite sthitiṃ yāti |
children.translated_text: When water moves, the reflection of the sun moves; when it is still, it becomes still;

children.text: antaḥkaraṇe gacchati gacchaty ātmāpi tadvad iha ||
children.translated_text: so too here, when the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) moves, the Self also appears to move.

children.text: rāhur adṛśyo 'pi yathā śaśibimbasthaḥ prakāśate jagati |
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Rāhu</s>, though invisible, becomes visible in the world when present in the orb of the moon,
so too the Self, though all-pervading, becomes visible when situated in the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>).

children.text: sarvagataṃ nirupamam advaitaṃ tac cetasā gamyam |
children.translated_text: That [<s>Brahman</s>] is all-pervading, incomparable, non-dual, and accessible through the mind;

children.text: yad buddhigataṃ brahmopalabhyate śiṣya bodhyaṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: O disciple, that <s>Brahman</s> which is grasped through the intellect — that is to be known.
Intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), mind (<s>manas</s>), ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), the groups of subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>) and sense organs, and the group of gross elements —
these, capable of creating and sustaining <s>saṃsāra</s>, are products of <s>Prakṛti</s> and are to be abandoned.
<s>Dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, the imagining of pleasure and pain, dwelling in heaven and hell,
birth, death, <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), and <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) — these do not exist in ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>).

children.text: mṛgatṛṣṇāyām udakaṃ śuktau rajataṃ bhujaṃgamo rajjvām |
children.translated_text: Water in a mirage, silver in a shell, a snake in a rope —
like the double moon seen by one with an eye-disease, the entire form of the world is [mere] delusion.

children.text: yadvad dinakara eko vibhāti salilāśayeṣu sarveṣu |
children.translated_text: Just as the one sun shines in all bodies of water,
so too the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), situated in all limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), shines.

children.text: kham iva ghaṭādiṣv antar bahiḥ sthitaṃ brahma sarvapiṇḍeṣu |
children.translated_text: Like space in pots and the like, <s>Brahman</s> exists inside and outside all bodies.
The notion 'I' in the body, which is not the Self, leads to the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Free from all conceptual constructions, pure, awakened, free from old age and death, peaceful,

children.text: amalaḥ sakṛd vibhātaś cetana ātmā khavad vyāpī ||
children.translated_text: stainless, self-luminous, conscious — the Self (<s>Ātman</s>) is all-pervading like space.
Just as juice, raw sugar, crystallized sugar, molasses, and sugar candy are modifications of sugarcane,
so too the various states are manifold modifications within the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) alone.
<s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>Antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath), <s>Virāj</s> (cosmic form), body, class, and individual —
these conventional designations are but particular states of that Self.

children.text: rajjvāṃ nāsti bhujaṃgaḥ sarpabhayaṃ bhavati hetunā kena |
children.translated_text: There is no snake in the rope — by what cause does the fear of a serpent arise?

children.text: tadvad dvaitavikalpabhrāntir avidyā na satyam idam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, the delusion of dualistic conceptualization is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — this [duality] is not real.

children.text: etat tad andhakāraṃ yad anātmany ātmatā bhrāntyā |
children.translated_text: This is that darkness: the [mistaken attribution of] selfhood to the non-self through delusion;

children.text: na vidanti vāsudevaṃ sarvātmānaṃ narā mūḍhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: deluded people do not know <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Self of all.
Having spread himself out through infinite divisions such as <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and others, like a net,
<s>Vāsudeva</s> withdraws [all], as if playing, through his own divine power (<s>vibhūti</s>).
By just three — <s>Viśva</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Prājña</s>, known as the beginning, middle, and end —
through waking, dream, and deep sleep, which are mere delusions, the <s>Turīya</s> (fourth state) is concealed.
The Lord (<s>Deva</s>) appears to delude himself through his own <s>māyā</s>, which has the form of duality,

children.text: upalabhate svayam evaṃ guhāgataṃ puruṣam ātmānam ||
children.translated_text: and perceives himself the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Self, that has entered the cave [of the heart].

children.text: jvalanād dhūmodgatibhir vividhākṛtir ambare yathā bhāti |
children.translated_text: Just as from fire, through rising smoke, various forms appear in the sky,

children.text: tadvad viṣṇau sṛṣṭiḥ svamāyayā dvaitavistarā bhāti ||
children.translated_text: so too from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, through his own <s>māyā</s>, the expanse of duality appears as creation.

children.text: śānta iva manasi sānte hṛṣṭe hṛṣṭa iva mūḍha iva mūḍhe |
children.translated_text: When the mind is calm, [the Self appears] as if calm; when it is joyful, as if joyful; when it is deluded, as if deluded —

children.text: vyavahārastho na punaḥ paramārthata īśvaro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: yet in ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) does not belong to the realm of conventional activity.
Just as the sky is not made impure by clouds, mist, smoke, or rising [dust],
so too the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> is untouched by the modifications of <s>Prakṛti</s>.

children.text: eksaminn api ca ghaṭe dhūmādimalavṛte śeṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even when one pot is covered with smoke and other impurities, the remaining [pots]

children.text: na bhavanti malopetā yadvad jīvo 'pi tadvad iha ||
children.translated_text: are not affected by impurity — so too is the case with the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) here.

children.text: dehendriyeṣu niyatāḥ karma guṇāḥ kurvate svabhogārtham |
children.translated_text: The <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), confined to the body and senses, perform actions for their own enjoyment;

children.text: nāhaṃ kartā na mameti jānataḥ karma naiva badhnāti ||
children.translated_text: for one who knows 'I am not the doer, [this is] not mine,' <s>karma</s> does not bind at all.

children.text: anyaśarīreṇa kṛtaṃ karma bhaved yena deha utpannaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> that was performed in another body, by which [the present] body has arisen —

children.text: tad avaśyaṃ bhoktavyaṃ bhogād eva kṣayo 'sya nirdiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that must necessarily be experienced; its destruction is declared to be through experience alone.
The <s>karma</s> accumulated prior to the arising of knowledge, which is consumed by the flame of knowledge,

children.text: bījam iva dahanadagdhaṃ janmasamarthaṃ na tad bhavati ||
children.translated_text: like a seed burnt by fire, is no longer capable of producing birth.

children.text: jñānotpatter ūrdhvaṃ kriyamānaṃ karma yat tad api nāma |
children.translated_text: And as for the <s>karma</s> performed after the arising of knowledge,

children.text: na śliṣyati kartāraṃ puṣkarapattraṃ yathā vāri ||
children.translated_text: it does not cling to the doer, just as water [does not cling] to a lotus leaf.

children.text: vāgdehamānasair iha karmacayaḥ kriyata iti buddhāḥ prāhuḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise declare that the accumulation of <s>karma</s> is produced here through speech, body, and mind.

children.text: eko 'pi nāham eṣāṃ kartā tatkarmaṇāṃ nāsmi ||
children.translated_text: 'Even [being] one, I am not the doer of these; I am not [the performer] of those actions.'
From the destruction of the seed of the fruit of <s>karma</s>, there is the destruction of birth — and there is no doubt in this.
Having realized this, one whose darkness has departed shines forth like the sun, radiant in nature.

children.text: yadvad iṣīkātūlaṃ pavanoddhūtaṃ hi daśa diśo yāti |
children.translated_text: Just as reed-cotton, blown by the wind, goes in all ten directions,
so too do the <s>karmas</s> of one who possesses true knowledge [scatter and dissipate] through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: kṣīrād uddhṛtam ājyaṃ kṣiptaṃ yadvan na pūrvavat tasmin |
children.translated_text: Just as ghee extracted from milk, when poured back, does not become [milk] as before,
so too the conscious Self, once separated from the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s>, [does not return to bondage].
Having shaken off the dense [forest of] <s>māyā</s> composed of the <s>guṇas</s>, just as the thousand-rayed [sun dispels] darkness,
the <s>Puruṣa</s>, moving both externally and internally, becomes like a solid mass of salt [— uniformly conscious throughout].

children.text: yadvad deho 'vayavā mṛd eva tasya vikārajātāni |
children.translated_text: Just as the body [of a pot] and its parts are nothing but clay, and its various modifications [are clay],
so too the moving and unmoving [world], though non-dual (<s>advaita</s>), appears as if dual.
From one <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), many classes of <s>kṣetrajñas</s> have arisen,
like sparks [flying] in all directions from fire that has entered iron.

children.text: te guṇasaṃgamadoṣād baddhā iva dhānyajātayaḥ svatuṣaiḥ |
children.translated_text: They, through the fault of association with the <s>guṇas</s>, are bound as if like varieties of grain by their own husks,

children.text: janma labhante tāvad yāvan na jñānavahninā dagdhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and take birth until they are burned by the fire of knowledge.
The three <s>guṇas</s>, [abiding] in the Self that is consciousness, all-pervading, established, the support of all —

children.text: kurute sṛṣṭim avidyā sarvatra spṛśyate tayā nātmā ||
children.translated_text: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) creates this creation; yet by it, the Self is not touched anywhere.

children.text: rajjvāṃ bhujaṃgahetuḥ prabhavavināśau yathā na staḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the cause of [seeing] a snake in a rope — its origination and destruction — do not [truly] exist,

children.text: jagadutpattivināśau na ca kāraṇam asti tadvad iha ||
children.translated_text: so too here, the origination and destruction of the world [do not truly exist], and there is no [real] cause.
Eternally free from birth, destruction, going, coming, impurity, and connection,
like space in pots and the like, the Self of all is present everywhere at all times.
The connection with the auspicious and inauspicious fruits of <s>karma</s>, with pleasure and pain, belongs to the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>);
from association with them comes bondage, like a non-thief [being bound] through association with thieves.
As long as the <s>Puruṣa</s> has association with the body, <s>guṇas</s>, organs, and sense-objects here,

children.text: tāvan māyāpāśaiḥ saṃsāre baddha iva bhāti ||
children.translated_text: so long does he appear as if bound in <s>saṃsāra</s> by the nooses of <s>māyā</s>.
Deluded by the distinctions of mother, father, son, relatives, wealth, and enjoyment,
the creature revolves as on a wheel in [this cycle] consisting of birth, old age, and death.
Those deluded ones who here worship the <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) produced by worldly convention,
they, subject to birth and death, having entered blinding darkness, suffer.

children.text: himaphenabudbudā iva jalasya dhūmo yathā vahneḥ |
children.translated_text: Like frost, foam, and bubbles [are modifications] of water, and smoke of fire,
so too this <s>māyā</s> is declared to be the inherent nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Thus, having abandoned <s>māyā</s>, which consists of dualistic conceptualization, whose nature is delusion, and which is bewildering,
one should meditate upon <s>Brahman</s>, which is non-dual, whole, and partless.

children.text: yadvat salile salilaṃ kṣīre kṣiraṃ samīraṇe vāyuḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as water merges into water, milk into milk, wind into wind,

children.text: tadvad brahmaṇi vimale bhāvanayā tanmayatvam upayāti ||
children.translated_text: so too, through meditation, one attains identity with the pure <s>Brahman</s>.
When thus, through meditation, the entire mass of duality has attained the state of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: ko mohaḥ kaḥ śokaḥ sarvaṃ brahmāvalokayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: what delusion remains, what grief, for one who sees everything as <s>Brahman</s>?

children.text: vigatopādhiḥ sphaṭikaḥ svaprabhayā bhāti nirmalo yadvat |
children.translated_text: Just as a crystal, freed from limiting adjuncts, shines pure with its own radiance,
so too the light of consciousness, free from <s>upādhis</s> (limiting adjuncts), shines here with its own radiance.
By the multitude of qualities, the senses, the body, the vital breaths, the subtle elements, birth, pleasure and pain —
untouched, all-pervading, of the nature of consciousness, this [self] is always pure.

children.text: draṣṭā śrotā ghrātā sparśayitā rasayitā grahītā ca |
children.translated_text: The seer, hearer, smeller, toucher, taster, and grasper —
the embodied one, devoid of body, senses, and intellect, is not an agent.
One, not stationed in any particular place, I am pervading all this through the power of sovereignty,

children.text: ākāśavad akhilam idaṃ na kaścid apy atra saṃdehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like space; there is no doubt whatsoever about this.
When one truly contemplates that this entire [universe] is the self alone — both partless and having parts —
freed from the dense forest of delusion, one becomes the supreme lord at that very moment.
Whatever those blinded by passion declare in established doctrines (<s>siddhāntas</s>), scriptures (<s>āgamas</s>), and reasonings (<s>tarkas</s>),
all that we approve, with the understanding that all doctrines speak of the universal self.

children.text: sarvākāro bhagavān upāsyate yena yena bhāvena |
children.translated_text: The all-formed <s>Bhagavān</s> — in whatever manner one worships him,

children.text: taṃ taṃ bhāvaṃ bhūtvā cintāmaṇivat samabhyeti ||
children.translated_text: he assumes that very form and approaches, like a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>).
Having known <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as the self, the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution,
one becomes omniscient, omnipresent, all, and the lord of all.

children.text: ātmajñas tarati śucaṃ yasmād vidvān bibheti na kutaścit |
children.translated_text: The knower of the self crosses over grief; therefore the wise one fears nothing whatsoever.

children.text: mṛtyor api maraṇabhayaṃ na bhavaty anyat kutas tasya ||
children.translated_text: Even death has no fear of death for him — what else could there be?
Eternally free from decay, growth, slaying, being slain, bondage, and liberation —

children.text: paramārthatattvam etad yad ato 'nyat tad anṛtaṃ sarvam ||
children.translated_text: this is the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha tattva</s>); whatever is other than this is entirely unreal.
Thus, having known <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit), with the web of mental constructions dispelled,
delighting in the self (<s>ātmārāma</s>), established in tranquility, one becomes liberated (<s>kevalin</s>).
Just as reeds, plantains, bamboo, and sugarcane perish upon reaching their own flowering,
so too those born of their own nature perish upon attaining their essential nature.
When the knot of ignorance is cut, the host of doubts severed, merit (<s>śubha</s>) exhausted,

children.text: dagdhe ca janmabīje paramātmānaṃ hariṃ yāti ||
children.translated_text: and the seed of birth burnt — one attains the supreme self, <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: mokṣasya naiva kiṃcid dhāmāsti na cāpi gamanam anyatra |
children.translated_text: Liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) has no abode whatsoever, nor is there any going elsewhere.

children.text: ajñānamayagranther bhedo yas taṃ vidur mokṣam ||
children.translated_text: The breaking of the knot made of ignorance — that they know as liberation.

children.text: buddhvaivam asatyam idaṃ viṣṇor māyātmakaṃ jagadrūpam |
children.translated_text: Having understood that this world-form, consisting of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>māyā</s> (illusion), is unreal,
free from the pairs of opposites and unattached to the enjoyments of conditioned existence, one becomes peaceful.

children.text: buddhvā vibhaktāṃ prakṛtiṃ puruṣaḥ saṃsāramadhyago bhavati |
children.translated_text: Having known <s>Prakṛti</s> as separate, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, though dwelling in the midst of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
becomes freed from all actions, like a lotus leaf from water.

children.text: aśnan yadvā tadvā saṃvīto yena kenacic chāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: Eating whatever comes, clothed in whatever is available, peaceful,

children.text: yatra kvacana ca śāyī vimucyate sarvabhūtātmā ||
children.translated_text: sleeping wherever — the self of all beings is liberated.
Even if one performs thousands of horse-sacrifices, or commits sins equal to the killing of a Brahmin,

children.text: paramārthavin na puṇyair na ca pāpaiḥ spṛśyate vimalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the knower of the supreme truth, being pure, is touched neither by merit nor by sin.
Free from intoxication, anger, elation, jealousy, dejection, fear, and harshness in speech and thought,
without hymns of praise or ritual exclamations, one of unfathomable wisdom should move about as if inert.
Having thus realized the ultimate truth, which is free from origination and destruction,
one whose purpose is fulfilled and whose birth has borne fruit abides everywhere as one pleases.
The all-pervading, undivided, self of all, with all diversity dispelled,

children.text: nirupamaparamānandaṃ yo veda sa tanmayo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: incomparable, of supreme bliss — whoever knows this becomes one with it.

children.text: tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā naṣṭasmṛtir api parityajan deham |
children.translated_text: Whether at a sacred site or in the house of an outcaste, even having lost memory, abandoning the body,
liberated at the very moment of knowledge, one attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute isolation), with grief destroyed.
Visiting holy places leads to merit; dying at an outcaste's dwelling leads to hell.
But in the absence of the taint of merit and demerit — what [difference does] that [make]?

children.text: vṛkṣāgrāc cyutapādo yadvad anicchan naraḥ kṣitau patati |
children.translated_text: Just as a man who has slipped from a treetop falls to the ground even unwillingly,
so too the knower of <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>guṇas</s> attains liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) even unwillingly.
Having undertaken the practice of the path of the supreme truth, even without having attained <s>yoga</s>,
one enjoys the pleasures of the celestial worlds and rejoices with a delighted mind for a long time.

children.text: viṣayeṣu sārvabhaumaḥ sarvajanaiḥ pūjyate yathā rājā |
children.translated_text: Just as a king, sovereign over all objects of enjoyment, is honored by all people,
so too one who has fallen from <s>yoga</s> is honored by all gods in the worlds.

children.text: mahatā kālena mahān mānuṣyaṃ prāpya yogam abhyasya |
children.translated_text: After a great length of time, having obtained a great human birth and practiced <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: prāpnoti divyam amṛtaṃ yat tat paramaṃ padaṃ viṣṇoḥ ||
children.translated_text: one attains the divine nectar of immortality — that which is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: vedāntaśāstram akhilaṃ vilokya śeṣas tu jagadādhāraḥ |
children.translated_text: Having surveyed the entire <s>Vedānta-śāstra</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, the support of the world,
composed this <s>Paramārthasāra</s> (Essence of the Highest Truth) in eighty-five <s>āryā</s> verses.
